# Expose notebook-controller last-activity data for console consumption

## Description

Conditional epic: it exists only if the notebook activity data-sourcing investigation finds that the web console cannot read last-activity data through its current interfaces. In that outcome, this epic implements the exposure design that investigation produced in the notebook controller, so the console's idle-workbench report can read each workbench's last activity. Owned by the Workbenches team.

## Scope

- Implement the exposure change designed by the data-sourcing investigation: expose last-activity data on the interface the console can read, with the agreed "last activity" semantics (per-kernel vs per-workbench rollup, update behavior).
- Preserve existing culling behavior unchanged — the idle culler continues to stop workbenches after the configured inactivity period.
- No console-side work: the report itself is built by the console team; this epic only makes the data readable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the exposure design, the notebook controller exposes last-activity data readable by the console through its Kubernetes-API-based integration, with the agreed semantics; measured by the console reading the data for a sample of workbenches.
- Given the exposure change, existing culling behavior is unaffected; measured by culling continuing to stop idle workbenches per the configured inactivity period.
- The exposure change lands with tests covering the new data path.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): conditional enabler — required for the idle-workbench report only in the outcome where last-activity data is not already console-readable.

# Investigate notebook activity data sourcing for the idle-workbench report

## Description

The web console must render a per-project idle-workbench report showing each workbench's last activity, owner, and reserved resources, sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. The console reads component backends through the Kubernetes API only (it has no private component APIs), while the notebook controller tracks last activity per kernel through Jupyter server API probes for the idle culler — and it is not established where that activity data is stored or whether the console can read it through its current interfaces. This investigation determines what activity data exists, where it lives, and whether it is console-readable today; if it is not, it produces the exposure design the notebook controller needs so the report can be built. Run by the Workbenches team in collaboration with the console team.

## Scope

- Analyze the notebook controller (midstream fork) source and configuration: what last-activity data the culler tracks, where it is stored (controller memory, ConfigMap, Notebook CR status), and its semantics (per-kernel vs per-workbench rollup, update frequency).
- Determine whether that data is exposed on an interface the web console can read through its Kubernetes-API-based integration, citing controller source and CRD evidence.
- Confirm which report inputs the console already reads today for workbenches (owner, reserved resources) and that they need no producer-side change.
- If the data is not console-readable: produce an exposure design — what the controller should expose, on which interface, with agreed "last activity" semantics — sized to the idle-workbench report's needs.
- Record the outcome as one of two bounded decisions: exposure work needed, or already readable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the notebook controller source and its documented interfaces, the investigation documents where last-activity data is stored and whether the console can read it through its current interfaces, with source citations; measured by review of the written determination by the console and workbench teams.
- Given the finding that the data is not console-readable, an exposure design is produced naming what the controller would expose, on which interface, and the semantics of "last activity"; measured by design sign-off from both teams.
- Given the finding that the data is already readable, the exact existing fields and interface the idle-workbench report will use are identified and recorded.
- The outcome is recorded as a bounded decision (exposure needed vs. already readable) so planning can attach or drop the conditional notebook-controller exposure work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): enables the per-project idle-workbench report by resolving where its last-activity input comes from and whether producer-side exposure work is required.

# Investigate pipeline run metadata sourcing for the stale-run report

## Description

The web console must render a per-project stale pipeline-run report listing completed runs older than a configurable age together with their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. Pipeline runs are already surfaced in the console today, but the run completion timestamps and per-run artifact-retention information this report needs may not be part of what the console currently reads — Kubeflow Pipelines retains run metadata behind the KFP v2 REST API, and the console integrates with component backends through the Kubernetes API. This investigation determines what run completion and artifact-retention metadata exists, whether the console can read it through its current interfaces, and if not, produces the exposure design the pipelines stack needs. Run by the RHOAI Pipelines team in collaboration with the console team.

## Scope

- Analyze what the console currently reads to surface pipeline runs, and identify the gap against the stale-run report's inputs (completion timestamps, per-run retained artifacts).
- Determine where Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata and artifact information, and whether the console can read it through its current interfaces, citing API and source evidence.
- If the data is not console-readable: produce an exposure design for the pipelines stack — what would be exposed, on which interface — sized to the stale-run report's needs.
- Record the outcome as one of two bounded decisions: exposure work needed, or already readable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the KFP v2 API surface and the console's current pipeline-run integration, the investigation documents what run completion and artifact-retention metadata exists and whether the console can read it through its current interfaces, with citations; measured by review of the written determination by the console and pipelines teams.
- Given the finding that the data is not console-readable, an exposure design is produced naming what the pipelines stack would expose and on which interface; measured by design sign-off from both teams.
- Given the finding that the data is already readable, the exact existing fields and interface the stale-run report will use are identified and recorded.
- The outcome is recorded as a bounded decision (exposure needed vs. already readable) so planning can attach or drop the conditional pipelines exposure work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): enables the stale pipeline-run report by resolving where its run completion and artifact inputs come from and whether producer-side exposure work is required.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the web console

## Description

Delivers the strategy's core capability in the RHOAI web console: a per-project idle-workbench report and a per-project stale pipeline-run report, with CSV export of either report, giving cluster administrators the visibility they need to reclaim capacity with confidence. The reports are read-only views; reclamation itself remains a manual, admin-driven activity (automated reclamation and cost calculations are out of scope). This epic depends on the outcomes of the two data-sourcing investigations (notebook activity; pipeline run metadata): each report's data-reading approach is fixed by its investigation's outcome, and where an investigation finds producer-side exposure work is needed, the corresponding report builds against the newly exposed data once that work lands.

## Scope

- Idle-workbench report view, per project: for each workbench, last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking via the interface established as console-readable), owner, and reserved resources.
- Stale pipeline-run report view, per project: completed runs older than a configurable age, with their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata via the interface established as console-readable.
- Configurable staleness age threshold for the pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report.
- Per-project scoping consistent with the console's existing project context and access model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then it lists each workbench with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources; measured by report values matching the notebook controller's activity tracking for a sample of workbenches.
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then it lists completed runs older than the configured age with their retained artifacts; measured by report values matching Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for a sample of runs.
- Given a change to the configurable staleness age, when the stale pipeline-run report is viewed, then the listed runs reflect the new threshold.
- Given either report, when an administrator exports it, then a CSV of the report's rows is produced.
- Given the data-sourcing outcomes, the reports read data only through the interfaces those investigations established as console-readable; where producer-side exposure work was required, the corresponding report is verified against the exposed data after that work lands.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): delivers the per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources).
- HLR-2 (P1): delivers the per-project stale pipeline-run report with its configurable age threshold.
- HLR-3 (P2): delivers CSV export of either report — bundled here because it shares the reports' UI surfaces and data and is not independently deferrable.

# Document the idle/stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

Produces the user documentation for the new console reporting capability: what each report shows, where its data comes from, how to interpret idle and stale entries, how to export a report as CSV, and — critically for the strategy's goal — safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs. Reclamation guidance stays within the strategy's boundaries: manual steps only (automated reclamation and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope). This epic is sequenced after the console reports implementation so the documentation describes what was actually built.

## Scope

- Documentation topics explaining the idle-workbench report: what it lists (last activity, owner, reserved resources), its data source, and how to interpret it.
- Documentation topics explaining the stale pipeline-run report: completed runs past the configurable age threshold, their retained artifacts, and how to configure the threshold.
- Safe reclamation guidance: manual steps and cautions for reclaiming capacity from idle workbenches and from stale runs and their artifacts.
- CSV export usage for both reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains both reports and covers every user-visible element of the delivered reporting capability, including the configurable staleness age and CSV export; measured by a coverage check of the documentation against the implemented reports.
- Documentation includes step-by-step safe reclamation guidance for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope boundary (manual reclamation only, no cost calculations); measured by review of the reclamation steps against actual platform behavior.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports by the team that built them before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): delivers documentation explaining the reports and safe reclamation steps.
